subject: Accountancy
title: Daily High-Yield Focus: Capitalisation Method
content:
Question:

A firm earned average profits of ₹1,00,000 during the last few years. The normal rate of return in a similar business is 10%. The total assets of the firm are ₹11,00,000 and liabilities are ₹2,00,000. Calculate Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits Method.

Step-by-Step Solution:

1. Capitalised Value of Profits = (Average Profit × 100) / Normal Rate = (1,00,000 × 100) / 10 = ₹10,00,000

2. Net Assets = Total Assets - External Liabilities = 11,00,000 - 2,00,000 = ₹9,00,000

3. Goodwill = Capitalised Value - Net Assets = 10,00,000 - 9,00,000 = ₹1,00,000

quiz.question: Goodwill calculated under Capitalisation Method uses which formula?
options: Super Profit × Number of Years Purchase
Average Profit × Normal Rate of Return

subject: Business Studies
title: Daily Case Study: Functional Foremanship
content:
Case Scenario: Production Manager Rahul noticed low productivity due to lack of specialized supervision. Which technique of Taylor solves this issue?

Topper Answer:

Functional Foremanship. Taylor proposed 8 specialized bosses to separate planning from execution.

subject: Economics
title: Daily Numerical Focus: Real GDP vs Nominal GDP
content:
Question: If Real GDP is ₹500 and Price Index (GDP Deflator) is 125, calculate Nominal GDP.

Formula & Calculation:

GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100

125 = (Nominal GDP / 500) × 100 ➜ Nominal GDP = ₹625
